selected_problem: Fresh-main diagnosis still grants `resolves` authority to uncommitted or dirty evidence content. An untracked evidence file can therefore suppress a committed unresolved boundary even though the truth-boundary ledger treats committed resolution records as the provenance required to close older evidence.

execution.route_basis: The new main exposes one narrow, directly reproducible provenance-authority defect adjacent to the just-closed same-revision causality gap. It is central to trustworthy autonomous diagnosis, locally verifiable, and does not require a product form or architecture choice, so source-contract replay routes to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without forced rotation.

changes: Truth-boundary resolution references now gain suppression authority only when the evidence source exists at HEAD and is clean against HEAD.
Untracked, staged, or modified evidence may still be observed as workspace evidence, but its `resolves` entries cannot erase committed boundary rows.
Committed newer resolution evidence still suppresses explicitly referenced older rows; no semantic inference or roadmap encoding is introduced.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: REPRODUCED: with a committed `UNRESOLVED` row in `evidence/old.json`, adding an untracked `evidence/uncommitted.json` containing only a matching `resolves` reference made the previous bridge emit RuntimeError: NO_ACTIONABLE_CANDIDATE.

truth_boundaries: This gates only resolution authority; uncommitted evidence rows can still be visible as workspace observations and are not claimed to be canonical-main facts.
Git cleanliness is provenance for whether a `resolves` record may suppress older rows, not cryptographic authenticity or semantic proof of closure.
BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: GitHub's merge REST endpoint still lacks an atomic expected-base-SHA precondition, so external GET-to-PUT base races remain outside client-side elimination.
